newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end strongly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end strongly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended strongly higher on softer than expected manufacturing data which ignited a rally in bonds and on sentiment that interest rates will remain steady, floor traders said.

S&P 500 futures spiked higher at the opening, moving in tandem with bond futures, after the National Association of Purchasing Management reported its business index slipped to 55.7 in June from 57.1 in May. Analysts had expected a smaller decline to 56.4.

Traders had fretted that a surprisingly robust June Chicago purchasers index on Monday would foreshadow a stronger national number. However, such key components in the national report as production, new orders and prices paid all declined from the previous month.
Bond futures catapulted higher on the news, which in turn propelled stock futures upward, traders said.
September S&P 500 futures pushed above 900.00 in morning trade and later extended gains to a session high of 903.25 after a late-session dip provided a buying opportunity for some investors.

The contract has struggled above 900.00 in recent sessions and appears to be forming a flag pattern on daily bar charts which could set the stage for a decisive surge above the stubborn level, a technical analyst said.

Stalling at a round-number benchmark and trading sideways for a few days before ultimately pushing through and continuing the march into uncharted territory is typical behavior for both the Dow industrials and S&Ps these days, he noted.
"I would say the safe bet is to go for an upside move here," the analyst said.
Bullishness was also tied to sentiment the Federal Open Market Committee will conclude its two-day meeting on Wednesday without changing interest rates, stock traders said.
"There is no one in the world who believes they will raise rates," a stock index floor trader said.

Thursday, a shortened trading day for index futures, brings the June U.S. employment data. Markets are closed Friday for the July 4 holiday. Nonfarm payrolls are seen rising 222,000, compared with a gain of 138,000 in May, and the unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 4.8 percent.

Sept S&Ps ended up 11.00 at 901.25, NYSE Composites up 5.25 at 470.85, Nikkeis down 310 at 20,285, Midcap 400s up 3.15 at 292.75, Nasdaq 100s up 0.95 at 967.45 and Russell 2000s down 1.00 at 397.90. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
